sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: hook h11 (notes/hooks.md), sketch i08, caller. Medium target, Hard welcome (user,
  2026-10-10: no Easy slot). Platform: rev 0 Run 1 "Between levels", Low 0/5 · Medium 5/5 (## Platform
  validation); rev 1 quick test "too easy" (Feedback log). Rev 2 restores the part of rev 0 that rev 1
  dropped, the valid letters on the June order, and keeps a derived-date order side. Measured result for
  rev 2 pending.
- Why rev 2 restores the order letters: rev 0 stopped the easier solver six draws out of six (five in Run 1,
  one quick test) and rev 1 failed to on its first draw. The rule side was word for word the same in both.
  What rev 1 removed was "21 letters on its June 21 Ebola entry order", the group that makes a letter look
  like an ordinary, accepted comment; without it "letters" stood out against "portal comments". That reading
  is an inference from seven draws with one trace; the other possibility is that the method slip is a
  matter of chance per attempt.
- Dependency plan: Doc 4 L30, L33-34, L39 (rule: received by June 26; portal only; electronic). Doc 5 L39
  (comments on the original and Amended Orders accepted "through June 22, 2026"), L27 (June order: comments
  on or before July 10), L29-32 (portal or mail). Doc 6 L27 (July order: on or before July 31). Doc 7 L27-28
  (August order: on or before September 1). Arrival dates, 20 days after the prior order's comments closed:
  June 22 gives July 12 (after July 10, out); July 10 gives July 30 (before July 31, in); July 31 gives
  August 20 (before September 1, in). Rule: 30 letters out, 18 portal comments of June 25 in. June order
  letters of June 25: in. 18 + 21 + 19 + 12 = 70.
- Universe: six groups, 122 comments in all (30 + 18 + 21 + 22 + 19 + 12); 70 accepted, 52 not (30 + 22).
- Necessity: Doc 4 is the only document with the rule's portal-only method and June 26 date. Doc 5 is the
  only document with the June order's deadline (July 10), which both rules out the June batch and dates the
  July batch, and with that order's mail method. Doc 6 is the only document with the July order's deadline
  (July 31); Doc 7 gives that order only "a 15-day comment period", which from July 13 gives July 28 and
  would drop the July batch (51) and date the August batch from the wrong day. Doc 7 is the only document
  that prints the August order and its deadline. The June 22 date is in Doc 5, Doc 6 and Doc 7 alike. No
  document has only an excluding role, so all four are answer components. The wording states no rule, no
  deadline and no closing date.
- Selected-lever checks (Python, 2026-10-10): gold 18 + 21 + 19 + 12 = 70. Order's mail rule carried to the
  rule: 100. June batch counted (an order in force taken as open for comment): 92; with the letters: 122.
  Lag counted from each order's issue date, or from the prior order's end instead of its comment close: only
  the August batch survives, 51. The 15-day label for the July order (July 28): 51. Portal-only carried to
  the June order (its letters dropped): 49. The three lag results hold if the 20 days are miscounted by a
  day either way (July 11 to 13, July 29 to 31, August 19 to 21), so no answer turns on a counting
  convention.
- Targeted failure modes: mode 1 (Wrong jurisdiction or scope, misapplies a rule or premise) -> 100, the
  order's mail rule applied to the interim rule. Measured on rev 0 Run 1: all five low attempts counted the
  30 letters (answer 91 there). Considered and not declared, nothing observed: an order in force taken as
  open for comment (92) and the wrong base date for the lag (51). Re-declare from rev 2's observed wrong
  answers before Submit.
- Calculation verification: Python datetime 2026-10-10: June 22 plus 20 days is July 12; July 10 plus 20 days
  is July 30; July 31 plus 20 days is August 20. 18 + 21 = 39; 39 + 19 = 58; 58 + 12 = 70. Each batch also
  arrives after its own order was issued (June 21, July 13, August 12).
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: no document prints 70, the arrival dates or the scenario's counts. Shortest
  route: the rule's DATES and ADDRESSES; the June order's ADDRESSES; four comment-closing dates (June 22,
  July 10, July 31, September 1) from three orders; three date additions; one sum.
- Precision/readings: "the prior order" of the June order is the Amended Order of May 22 (with the original
  order), whose comments Doc 5 says were accepted through June 22; of the July order, the June 21 order; of
  the August order, the July 13 order. "Comments closed" is the last day comments were accepted, not the day
  the order stopped being in effect (July 21, August 12), which the notices print separately. "Its June,
  July and August orders" are the orders issued June 21, July 13 and August 12. "Letters" are mailed paper
  comments. Labelling instructions are outside "method and timing".
- Completeness: full corpus, no gaps (notes/intake.json; notes/doc-map.md coverage lines).
- Style/set review: 60 words, one ask; at the form's warning line (over 60 warns). No other live question in
  the bundle.
- Scenario numbers: 30, 18, 21, 22, 19 and 25 are printed in digits in Doc 5, 12 in Doc 6 and Doc 7, and 20
  in Doc 7 (character 16,106) and Doc 6 (19,561), so the form's number check has a document for each.
- Revision history: rev 2 (2026-10-10) answers the quick-test report on rev 1 (Feedback log; index F8).
  Changed from rev 1: the 21 letters on the June order restored; the order batches now 22, 19 and 12, timed
  from the prior order's comment close (20 days) instead of from each order's issue date (19 days); gold 52
  to 70; all four documents answer components (rev 1 had Doc 6 as an exclusion source); Steps 3-13 and
  evidence. Unchanged since rev 0: the rule side, the closing question, the failure-mode pair. Rev 1 (gold
  52, d8855b69...) answered Run 1 on rev 0. Stop rule: if rev 2 is too easy at the quick test, or Between
  levels again with the medium model at 4 or 5 of 5, this hook has no Medium form and release is
  recommended.
- Coach suggestions on rev 0, checked against the text: (1) relative descriptions instead of explicit dates:
  adopted for the order batches. (2) asking which requirement each failing group broke: not adopted, it
  makes two asks and a long answer.
- Warnings answered: floor run recorded at hand-over (rev 2).

sections.question: On June 25, 2026, CDC received 30 letters and 18 portal comments on its interim quarantine rule and 21 letters on its June 21 Ebola entry order. Later, 22, 19 and 12 portal comments reached its June, July and August orders, each 20 days after comments closed on the prior order. How many met CDC's requirements on method and timing?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 4, DATES and ADDRESSES): comments on the interim final rule must be received by June 26, 2026. They may be submitted by one method only, the Federal eRulemaking Portal, and all comments must be submitted electronically.

Step 2. Application (Doc 4 and Doc 5): the 30 letters on the rule were not submitted electronically, so they do not meet the rule's method requirement. The 18 portal comments on the rule arrived on June 25, before June 26, and count.

Step 3. Source input (Doc 5, SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION, DATES and ADDRESSES): CDC accepted comments on the original and Amended Orders, the orders before the June 21, 2026 order, through June 22, 2026. Comments on the June 21 order may be submitted through the portal or by mail and must be received on or before July 10, 2026.

Step 4. Application (Doc 4 and Doc 5): the 21 letters on the June order came by mail, a method that order accepts, on June 25, before July 10, and count.

Step 5. Calculation (Doc 5 and Doc 7): June has 30 days, so the days of June left after June 22 are 30 - 22 = 8.

Step 6. Calculation (Doc 5 and Doc 7): the rest of the 20 days fall in July: 20 - 8 = 12. The June order's batch arrived on July 12, after July 10, so its 22 comments do not count.

Step 7. Source input (Doc 6, DATES): written comments on the July order must be received on or before July 31, 2026.

Step 8. Calculation (Doc 5, Doc 6 and Doc 7): comments on the order before the July order closed on July 10, so the July order's batch arrived on this day of July: 10 + 20 = 30. July 30 is before July 31, so its 19 comments count.

Step 9. Source input (Doc 7, DATES): written comments on the August order must be received on or before September 1, 2026.

Step 10. Application (Doc 6 and Doc 7): comments on the order before the August order closed on July 31, the last day of July, so the August order's batch arrived 20 days into August, on August 20. That is before September 1, so its 12 comments count.

Step 11. Calculation (Doc 4 and Doc 5): the rule's timely portal comments plus the June order's letters: 18 + 21 = 39.

Step 12. Calculation (Doc 5 and Doc 6): adding the July order's batch: 39 + 19 = 58.

Step 13. Calculation (Doc 6 and Doc 7): adding the August order's batch: 58 + 12 = 70.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Wrong jurisdiction or scope
How a careless solver fails: Misapplies a rule or premise

Why these are traps: Wrong jurisdiction or scope: Doc 5's order accepts mailed comments, and the question's own letters on that order count, but Doc 4's interim rule takes comments only through the portal. Carrying the order's mail rule to the rule counts its 30 letters: 100. The rule's own terms give 70.
